title: Answer of Foundry Works Solar Energy LLC in response to comments filed by Just Transition Northwest Indiana on 09/23/2026 under ER26-3713.

UNITED STATES OF AMERICA
                                      BEFORE THE
                        FEDERAL ENERGY REGULATORY COMMISSION


    Foundry Works Solar Energy LLC                           )                      Docket No. ER26-3713-000

                     ANSWER OF FOUNDRY WORKS SOLAR ENERGY LLC

           Pursuant to Rules 212 and 213 of the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission’s

(“Commission”) Rules of Practice and Procedure,1 Foundry Works Solar Energy LLC (“Foundry

Works”) respectfully moves for leave to answer2 and submits this answer in response to the

comments filed by Just Transition Northwest Indiana (“JTNWI”) on September 23, 2026.3

           JTNWI presents what it characterizes as additional land-use and interconnection facts

related to Foundry Works’ project and requests the Commission take such facts into account in

considering Foundry Works’ Waiver Request.4 While Foundry Works appreciates local

engagement in this proceeding, nothing in JTNWI’s comments negates the showing in Foundry

Works’ Waiver Request that good cause exists for the Commission to grant the requested waiver

and extend Foundry Works’ commercial operation date (“COD”) to allow the project to deliver

much-needed capacity.




1
    18 C.F.R. §§ 385.212 and 213.
2
 Although the Commission’s regulations generally do not allow for an answer to a comment, the Commission
routinely permits such answers when they provide useful information that will assist the Commission in its decision-
making process, for example, such as here, by clarifying the record. See e.g., New England Power Generators
Association, Inc. v. ISO New England Inc., 175 FERC ¶ 61,177 at P 52 (2021); PJM Interconnection, L.L.C. and XO
Energy, LLC, XO Energy MA, LP, and XO Energy MA2, LP v. PJM Interconnection, L.L.C., 175 FERC ¶ 61,137 at
P 25 (2021); Invenergy Solar Development North America LLC v. Tri-State Generation and Transmission Assoc.,
Inc., 174 FERC ¶ 61,184 at P 55 (2021).
3
 Just Transition Northwest Indiana Comments, Docket No. ER26-3713-000 (filed Sept. 23, 2026) (“JTNWI
Comments”).
4
  Foundry Works Solar Energy LLC, Request for Prospective Tariff Waiver and Expedited Action, Docket No.
ER26-3713-000 (filed Sept. 3, 2026) (“Waiver Request”).

                                                         1
            Foundry Works reiterates its request that the Commission grant its Waiver Request by

October 19, 2026.

           I.      ANSWER

           As explained in its Waiver Request, Foundry Works is developing a 200 megawatt (“MW”)

battery energy storage system (“BESS” or the “Project”) that will be used to serve the growing

load of Indianapolis Power & Light Company d/b/a AES Indiana (“AES Indiana”). The Midwest

region faces critical resource adequacy challenges, with the North American Electric Reliability

Corporation classifying it as “high risk” beginning in 2028 due to surging demand from data

centers, artificial intelligence, and other large loads.5 AES Indiana, in particular, has an

accelerating and material capacity need driven by both baseline load growth and incremental large-

load demand, and projects like Foundry Works are essential to meeting these near-term reliability

requirements.6

           Foundry Works is actively developing its Project to help alleviate these resource adequacy

challenges. Foundry Works has already invested tens of millions of dollars in the Project, secured

100% of the needed land rights, funded the necessary network upgrades, and obtained

Midcontinent Independent System Operator, Inc.’s (MISO) approval to convert its interconnection

queue position to a 200 MW BESS—demonstrating Foundry Works’ commitment and readiness

to deliver much-needed capacity. Granting the Waiver Request will ensure that Foundry Works

meets AES Indiana’s critical energy needs, while at the same time avoiding the negative

consequences should the waiver request be denied, including that AES Indiana would face a

compressed timeline to procure replacement capacity at higher cost, pressuring customer rates


5
 North American Electric Reliability Corp, Long-Term Reliability Assessment, at 15, 27 (Jan. 23, 2026), available
at https://www.nerc.com/globalassets/our-work/assessments/nerc_ltra_2025.pdf.
6
    See Waiver Request at 5-6.

                                                        2
 upward. JTNWI’s comments do not undermine the showing Foundry Works has made in support

of its request.

          A.      Foundry Works Is On Track to Reach COD by December 15, 2028.

          JTNWI asserts that certain outstanding local permits and alleged infrastructure delays call

into question whether Foundry Works can achieve COD by December 15, 2028.7 These arguments

mischaracterize both the status of the Project and the applicable legal standard.

          The Commission routinely grants COD waivers where permits are pending and

construction is ongoing,8 recognizing that such activities are inherent features of large-scale energy

development. What matters, in evaluating a waiver request, is whether the developer has

demonstrated that the Commission’s four-part waiver criteria are met, which is precisely what

Foundry Works did here. Foundry Works explained in its Waiver Request that: (1) it acted in good

faith by diligently moving the Project forward, invested $38 million in the Project, secured 100%

of necessary land rights, obtained MISO’s approval for the fuel change to a 200 MW BESS, and

funded network upgrades that are nearly complete; (2) the waiver is limited in scope to permit a

twelve month extension of the COD tailored to finish Project development; (3) granting waiver

would address a concrete problem that the Project’s Generator Interconnection Agreement

(“GIA”) would be terminated and interconnection rights lost for failure to reach COD at the

delineated time; and (4) no third parties would be harmed. JTNWI’s attempt to recast routine,

sequential permitting milestones as evidence of uncertainty is without merit. To the extent JTNWI

raises concerns about shared infrastructure at the Dinwiddie substation, those concerns relate to

facilities under the control of third parties, namely Northern Indiana Public Service Company LLC


7
    JTNWI Comments at 1-3.
8
 See e.g., Mustang Mile Solar Energy LLC, 191 FERC ¶ 61,039 (2025); Grandview Solar Project LLC, 186 FERC ¶
61,151 (2024).

                                                    3
 (“NIPSCO”). As explained below, Foundry Works’ permitting activities continue under normal

and routine circumstances; there is no reason to believe at this time that the issues raised by JTNWI

will impede Project construction.

           As detailed in its Waiver Request, Foundry Works has made substantial and continuous

progress on local land approvals for the Project.9 Foundry Works successfully rezoned the Project

site for BESS use as of June 9, 2026, and is currently pursuing the BESS Special Exception permit

in Q4 of 2026, with final construction permits anticipated to be issued in Q1 2027, after which

construction can commence.10 JTNWI observes that as of September 16, 2026, local land

approvals were not yet complete.11 That certain approvals remain in progress is entirely consistent

with the orderly, sequential permitting timeline set forth in the Waiver Request. Foundry Works’

BESS Special Exception application is proceeding through the permitting process. The deferral

referenced by JTNWI’s comments is to provide Foundry Works additional time to work on routine

engineering and mitigation plans that will be presented to the Lake County Planning Commission

on October 21, 2026. These are standard permitting steps and Foundry Works does not anticipate

that the Lake County Planning Commission’s consideration of the local land approvals at its

forthcoming meeting will affect the overall permitting schedule, which Foundry Works expects to

conclude in early 2027 after which Foundry Works can begin construction.12

           JTNWI further notes that NIPSCO has not yet submitted the Special Exception request for

the Dinwiddie Substation and raises concerns that other interconnection customers are facing



9
    Foundry Works Waiver Request at 6-7.
10
     Id.
11
     JTNWI Comments at 1-2.
12
  Foundry Works Waiver Request at 6-7 (“Foundry Works is currently preparing the application for a BESS Special
Exception permit, and it anticipates that the special exception permitting process will be completed by the fourth
quarter of 2026” with the overall permitting process ongoing through Q1 2027).

                                                        4
 construction scheduling issues at the substation.13 These concerns are misplaced. The substation

is owned and operated by NIPSCO, a party over which Foundry Works exercises no control.

Foundry Works understands that NIPSCO is in the process of seeking the substation Special

Exception, and plans to submit the application on or about October 10, 2026. Although Foundry

Works understands that NIPSCO has already completed 90-95% of the substation work, with only

two breakers and the incoming lines still to be installed, Lake County required NIPSCO to halt

these final construction activities pending approval of the Special Exception permit. That NIPSCO

is in the process of securing local substation permits does not obviate or diminish Foundry Works’

need for the requested waiver.

           Further, JTNWI’s allegations regarding substation construction activities appear to relate

to work being performed on behalf of other interconnection customers14—not Foundry Works or

the Project. There is no reason to believe that work for other interconnection customers will impact

Foundry Works’ ability to achieve COD by December 15, 2028. However, to the extent any third-

party delays at the Dinwiddie Substation were to affect the Project’s timeline, such delays would

constitute circumstances outside Foundry Works’ control, further supporting—rather than

undermining—the basis for the requested waiver.

           B.       Foundry Works’ Conversion to BESS Was a Prudent Response to Changed
                    Reliability Conditions.

           Foundry Works’ conversion from a solar resource to a BESS was driven by circumstances

outside its control.15 When Foundry Works entered MISO queue in 2018, it did so as a solar project

consistent with the resource adequacy landscape at that time. In the intervening years, however,



13
     JTNWI Comments at 1-2, 3.
14
     JTNWI Comments at 3.
15
     Waiver Request at 7.

                                                   5
 the resource adequacy environment in the Midwest underwent a fundamental transformation

driven by unprecedented load growth from data centers, artificial intelligence, and other large

loads—developments that were not reasonably foreseeable at the time of queue entry. These shifts

prompted load-serving entities such as AES Indiana to identify an acute and growing need for

dispatchable, high-capacity resources, particularly BESS, to maintain reliability. Foundry Works’

conversion from solar to a 200 MW BESS was a direct and prudent response to AES Indiana’s

need for dispatchable capacity.

          Indeed, once the need for BESS became apparent, Foundry Works acted expeditiously: it

requested the fuel change from MISO, obtained MISO’s approval, secured the Conditional

Development rezone from Lake County on June 9, 2026, and is actively advancing the BESS

Special Exception permit, as well as other Project development activities. The requested extension

is necessary to allow sufficient time to complete development and construction of the resource the

region now requires.

          C.      AES Indiana State Proceeding.

          Finally, JTNWI perceives a discrepancy between the Project’s COD as described by AES

Indiana (May 31, 2028) in the Indiana Utility Regulatory Commission proceeding and the

requested COD in the waiver filing (December 15, 2028),16 but there is no discrepancy. JTNWI

notes that an AES Indiana witness described Foundry Works as having a “May 31, 2028

commercial operation target” and that “Foundry was seeking federal flexibility toward 2029.”17

Nothing about these prior statements contradicts Foundry Works’ requested COD extension until

December 15, 2028. While Foundry Works aspires to complete the Project more quickly, it will



16
     JTNWI Comments at 2.
17
     JTNWI Comments at 2.

                                                  6
 not meet the current COD, and it is Foundry Works’ assessment, based on the anticipated

permitting timeline and the construction schedule thereafter, that the company will need until

December 15, 2028, to achieve COD. This is consistent with AES Indiana’s representations that

Foundry Works seeks flexibility toward 2029.

II.     REQUEST FOR EXPEDITED ACTION

        Foundry Works respectfully renews its request that the Commission issue an order granting

the requested relief by October 19, 2026. Foundry Works has executed an agreement that will

allow AES Indiana to purchase the company and use the Project to serve its customers. Pursuant

to this agreement, Foundry Works must have certainty as to its COD in order to meet a contractual

milestone by November 1, 2026. Failure to obtain timely Commission action could jeopardize the

acquisition agreement, which would in turn impair AES Indiana’s ability to procure the capacity

it needs to serve its customers and maintain reliability in its service territory.

III.    CONCLUSION

        For the foregoing reasons, Foundry Works respectfully requests that the Commission

accept this answer and consider the information herein and issue an order granting the requested

waiver of Article 2.3.1 of the GIA and Section 4.4.4 of Attachment X to the MISO Tariff by

October 19, 2026, to permit a commercial operation date of December 15, 2028.
